how emotion can affect memory processes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emotional valence of the to-be-remembered information affects both the familiarity and the recollection processes in the false recognition memory.
the emotional valence of the to-be-remembered material affects the production of false memories, and this effect is mainly mediated by recollection.
the emotional valence of the stimuli affects the recollection process and not the familiarity process, as suggested by the conceptual relatedness account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional valence affects the production of false recognition memory by influencing recollective processes.
emotional content affects the production of false memories by influencing the distinctiveness heuristic rather than the conceptual relatedness.
emotional content affects the production of false recognition memory by engaging distinctiveness heuristic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
negative emotional content can reduce false memory by engaging a distinctness heuristic.
the emotional valence of the studied material can affect the production of false memories.
the distinctiveness heuristic can be a more powerful explanation than the familiarity account for the effects of emotion on false memory.
